rump and uppertail coverts strongly barred dark (first-winter)

art.subject: American Herring Gull (Larus smithsonianus), first-winter, as seen on Korean coasts in winter: body plumage rather uniformly dark brown and densely mottled; head and neck grey-brown with fine streaks, often a little paler on the face; back and wing coverts brown with fine pale notches; tertials dark brown with narrow pale edges; underparts evenly brown; rump and uppertail coverts heavily barred dark brown so they look dark; tail almost entirely blackish-brown; primaries blackish-brown; bill blackish, sometimes with a paler pinkish base; iris dark; legs dull pink.
art.pose: standing on wet sand at the tideline, side view
art.scene: Korean east-coast sandy shore in winter (January), grey sea and cold overcast light; no people, buildings or text
views: first-winter, side view standing on wet sand: large robust gull, evenly sooty grey-brown head, body and upperparts with neat scaly pale fringes, plain brownish underparts, blackish bill developing a dull flesh-coloured base, dark eye, blackish-brown primaries, pink legs

first-winter, in flight seen squarely from above: head, body and tail in one line, long wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span with a slight bend at the wrist, pale panel on the inner primaries, blackish outer primaries, brown rump strongly barred dark, mostly blackish tail

adult winter, side view standing: white head and neck streaked brown, pale yellow iris, yellow bill with a red spot on the lower mandible, pale grey back and upperwing, black wingtips, white underparts and tail, pink legs
art.build: Large, robust gull, about the size of Vega Gull, with a sturdy body, rounded to slightly flattened crown and a fairly long, strong bill with a moderate gonys angle. Legs medium length, pink. At rest the primaries project moderately beyond the tail. In flight dark outer primaries with a paler window on the inner primaries, a dark-barred rump and an almost all-dark tail.
avoid: Do not paint a whitish rump or a white tail with a narrow dark band; those suit first-winter Vega Gull (Larus vegae), while this bird's rump looks dark and its tail is almost all dark.
Do not paint an adult with a grey back and yellow bill; the bird shown is a first-winter.
Do not make it small or slim like Black-tailed Gull.
